hook: The reason you're forgettable in conversations has almost nothing to do with what you said. It has everything to do with this.
topic: The memory effect — what makes people feel unforgettable
body:
**The reason some people leave conversations feeling forgettable has almost nothing to do with what they said. It has everything to do with whether the other person felt heard.**

Here's the mechanism. Memory for people isn't stored as a transcript of the conversation. It's stored as a feeling. And the feeling that encodes most strongly — the one that determines whether someone thinks about you after you've gone — is whether they felt genuinely attended to while you were there.

When someone leaves a conversation with you thinking "she really listened" — they don't mean you were quiet while they spoke. They mean they felt the quality of your attention. They felt that you were tracking not just their words but what those words meant to them.

That feeling is rare. Most people in conversations are partly listening and partly preparing their next contribution. You can feel that split attention even when you can't name it.

Close that split — give someone your full, unhurried attention for even four minutes — and you become, without exaggeration, one of the more memorable people they'll talk to that week.

Not because you were interesting. Because you made them feel interesting.

More on this is linked in my bio.
